Spanish professional [[basketball]] player for [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[Basketball Champions League]] (BCL). Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=11}}, he plays at the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position. ==Professional career== ===Real Madrid (2011–2016)=== Considered one of the best prospects of [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], Hernangómez played his first two seasons on its [[Real Madrid Baloncesto B|reserve team]]. In the summer of 2013, Hernangómez was [[loan (sports)|loaned]] by Real Madrid to [[CB Sevilla|Cajasol Sevilla]], extending his agreement for one more season in the next summer. On 17 July 2015, he returned to Real Madrid{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/169112/willy-hernangomez-officially-returns-to-real-madrid.html |title=Willy Hernangomez officially returns to Real Madrid |work=Sportando.com |date=17 July 2015 |access-date=8 July 2016}} and played for the senior team in 2015–16. In his lone full season for the senior team, he averaged 5.7 points and 3.3 rebounds in 34 games in the [[Liga ACB|Spanish ACB League]].{{cite web |url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Guillermo-Hernangomez-7204/stats/ |title=DraftExpressProfile: Guillermo Hernangomez |work=DraftExpress.com |access-date=10 November 2016 |archive-date=18 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170818133329/http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Guillermo-Hernangomez-7204/stats/ |url-status=dead }} ===New York Knicks (2016–2018)=== [[File:Willy Hernangomez (31828545273).jpg|thumb|left|Hernangómez with the [[New York Knicks|Knicks]] in 2017]] Hernangómez declared for the [[2015 NBA draft]], and was selected with the 35th overall pick by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. His rights were later traded to the [[New York Knicks]] on draft night, in exchange for two future second round draft choices and cash considerations.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-acquire-guillermo-hernangomez |title=Knicks Acquire Guillermo Hernangomez |work=NBA.com |date=26 June 2015 |access-date=26 June 2015}} On 8 July 2016, Hernangómez signed with the New York Knicks.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-sign-guillermo-willy-hernangomez |title=Knicks Sign Guillermo "Willy" Hernangomez |work=NBA.com |date=8 July 2016 |access-date=8 July 2016}} On 25 October 2016, he made his debut for the Knicks in their season opener, scoring four points in nine minutes off the bench in a 117–88 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899375 |title=Knicks vs. Cavaliers – Box Score |work=ESPN.com |date=25 October 2016 |access-date=25 October 2016}} On 7 November 2016, he was assigned to the [[Westchester Knicks]], New York's [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate. He was recalled later that day.{{cite web |url=http://www.marca.com/baloncesto/nba/2016/11/07/5820d3dd46163f76458b45cb.html |title=Los Knicks envían a Willy Hernangómez a entrenar a la NBDL |work=Marca.com |date=7 November 2016 |access-date=3 December 2016 |language=es}} Two days later, he had a season-best 14 points in a 110–96 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899556 |title=Carmelo Anthony scores 22 points, Knicks beat Nets 110-96 |date=9 November 2016 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=10 November 2016 |agency=Associated Press}} On 25 January 2017, he had a career-high 16 rebounds in a 103–95 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900109 |title=Barnes scores 23 to lead Mavericks over Knicks, 103-95 |work=ESPN.com |date=25 January 2017 |access-date=26 January 2017}} On 1 February 2017, he had 16 points and 16 rebounds in a 95–90 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899394 |title=Porzingis, subs rally Knicks to 95-90 victory over Nets |work=ESPN.com |date=1 February 2017 |access-date=2 February 2017}} On 15 February, he was named as a replacement on the World Team for the injured [[Emmanuel Mudiay]] in 2017 [[Rising Stars Challenge]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/02/15/knicks-willy-hernangomez-replaces-nuggets-emmanuel-mudiay-rising-stars |title=Knicks' Willy Hernangomez replaces Nuggets' Emmanuel Mudiay in BBVA Rising Stars Challenge |work=NBA.com |date=15 February 2017 |access-date=16 February 2017}} On 25 March 2017, he had a career-high 24 points and 13 rebounds in a 106–98 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900480 |title=Leonard, Aldridge help Spurs topple Knicks, 106-98 |work=ESPN.com |date=25 March 2017 |access-date=26 March 2017}} On 9 April 2017, he tied his career high with 24 points and grabbed 11 rebounds in a 110–97 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900574 |title=Raptors handle Knicks to clinch top-3 seed in East |work=ESPN.com |date=9 April 2017 |access-date=9 April 2017}} Five days later, he was named Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month for games played in April after leading all Eastern Conference rookies in rebounding (8.5 rpg) and ranked second in scoring (12.5 ppg).{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/04/14/willy-hernangomez-and-tyler-ulis-named-kia-rookies-month |title=New York Knicks' Willy Hernangomez, Phoenix Suns' Tyler Ulis named Kia Rookies of Month |work=NBA.com |date=14 April 2017 |access-date=14 April 2017}} At the season's end, he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie First Team]].{{cite web |last=Rohrbach |first=Ben |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/draymond-green-joel-embiid-headline-nbas-defensive-rookie-team-announcements-193946303.html |title=Draymond Green, Joel Embiid headline NBA's All-Defensive, All-Rookie team announcements |work=Yahoo.com |date=27 June 2017 |access-date=27 June 2017}} ===Charlotte Hornets (2018–2020)=== On 7 February 2018, Hernangómez was traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for [[Johnny O'Bryant III]] and two future second round draft picks.{{cite web |title=Hornets Acquire Center Willy Hernangomez From Knicks |url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-acquire-center-willy-hernangomez-knicks |website=NBA.com |access-date=7 February 2018 |date=7 February 2018}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2020–2023)=== On 30 November 2020, Hernangómez signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web |title=Pelicans sign Wenyen Gabriel and Willy Hernangómez |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-weynen-gabriel-and-willy-hernangomez |website=NBA.com |date=30 November 2020 |access-date=2 December 2020}} ===FC Barcelona (2023–2026)=== On 12 July 2023, Hernangómez signed a lucrative three-year deal with Spanish powerhouse [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]], after his former club [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] decided not to match the offer sheet as per the domestic league rule of ''tanteo'' rights.{{cite web |title=Willy Hernangómez, culer fins al 2026 |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.cat/ca/basquet/primer-equip/noticies/3587720/willy-hernangomez-culer-fins-al-2026 |website=FCBarcelona.cat |date=12 July 2023 |access-date=14 July 2023 |language=Catalan}} On 30 June 2026, Hernangómez left Barcelona upon the expiration of his contract.{{cite web | title=Willy Hernangómez leaving FC Barcelona | url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/4528780/willy-hernangomez-leaving-fc-barcelona | website=fcbarcelona.com | date=30 June 2026 | access-date=30 June 2026 }} ===Unicaja Málaga (2026–present)=== On July 27, 2026, Hernangómez signed a one–year contract with [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[Basketball Champions League]].{{Cite web|title=Willy Hernangómez set to sign with Unicaja Malaga|url=https://basketnews.com/news-252741-willy-hernangomez-signs-with-unicaja-malaga.html|website=basketnews.com|language=en}} ==National team career== ===Junior national team=== As a member of the junior national teams of Spain, Hernangómez played at the 2012 [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]], where he was named to the All-Tournament Team. He also played at the [[2011 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], where he won a gold medal, and at the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], where he won a silver medal, and was named to the All-Tournament Team. ===Senior national team=== He has also been a member of the senior [[Spain national basketball team]]. With Spain's senior national team, he played at the [[EuroBasket 2015]], where he won a gold medal, and at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]], where he won a bronze medal. He also played at the [[EuroBasket 2017]], where he won a bronze medal. In [[2019 FIBA World Cup]], he won another gold medal. At [[EuroBasket 2022]], Hernangómez and Spain won a surprising gold medal after defeating [[France men's national basketball team|France]] in the [[EuroBasket 2022 Final|final]], in which he had 14 points and 8 rebounds.{{Cite web |title=Germany's medal success at home could just be the start |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/news/germany-s-medal-success-at-home-could-just-be-the-start |access-date=2022-09-19 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} Hernangómez was named the [[EuroBasket MVP]] after averaging 17.2 points and 6.9 rebounds over the tournament.{{Cite web |title=Willy Hernangomez earns TISSOT MVP award to lead TISSOT All-Star Five in Berlin |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/news/willy-hernangomez-earns-tissot-mvp-award-to-lead-tissot-all-star-five-in-berlin |access-date=2022-09-19 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}
